title: implement-segmented-cursor-and-ttl-backed-inverted-time-index-for-dashboard-queries
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Background: Several dashboard endpoints (usage timeline, per-tenant cost breakdown, and per-route latency heatmaps) show tail latency spikes when users page through long time ranges (90d+) or when tenants have high cardinality (many models/routes). Current offset-based pagination and a single time-sorted partition require scanning large segments and touching cold shards. This ticket implements a new query plan and index structure to reduce latency and IO for deep pagination and heavy tenants.

Goals:
- Reduce 95th/99th percentile query latency for paginated dashboard endpoints by 40-60% for common large-range queries.
- Reduce read IO and query CPU for high-cardinality tenants via targeted indexes and prefetch.
- Maintain backward-compatible cursor semantics for clients; fail open to offset pagination as fallback.

Proposal summary:
1) Segmented result cursor: introduce a server-side cursor token that encodes (time_segment_id, shard_cursor, result_position, version). Cursors are opaque to clients but allow the backend to resume reads from a specific time-segment without re-scanning earlier segments. Cursors expire after 24h by default (configurable).
2) TTL-backed inverted-time index: build an inverted index keyed by (tenant_id, metric_route, time_bucket) -> sorted list of event pointers. Time buckets are variable-width (e.g., hourly for recent 7d, daily for 8-90d) to keep indexes small. Index entries have a TTL shard that allows compaction and keeps index size bounded.
3) Adaptive prefetcher: for cursor-based reads, prefetch the next N index blocks (configurable based on observed latency) in parallel and warm KV cache. Prefetch policy uses per-tenant heatmap (hot tenants get more aggressive prefetch).
4) Query planner changes: planner decides between three strategies: indexed-segment scan (preferred), reservoir-range scan (fallback for small ranges), and legacy offset-scan (last-resort compatibility). Planner picks based on estimated cardinality, time range, and tenant heat clazz.

Backward compatibility: clients sending page=offset will continue to work. New API will expose cursor token in responses; clients can opt-in. Server should accept either and internally translate offset requests into cursors where feasible.

Data migration: index build will run asynchronously via a reindex job that reads from the canonical event store and writes index shards to the new index table. A parallel backfill process will mark tenants as "index-ready" once their index coverage reaches 95% for the last 90 days. Until marked ready, planner may choose legacy strategies for those tenants.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for /dashboard/usage/timeline with 90d range decreases by >=40% in canary tenants
99th percentile latency decreases by >=30% for high-cardinality tenants in canary
Average read IO (GB) per large-range query decreases by >=25% in canary
Cursor tokens are opaque and expire; client-facing behavior unchanged unless client opts into cursor paging
Reindex/backfill job can process at least 50 tenants/hour in staging with current infra
Rollout toggle exists in runtime config and Console UI to enable cursor-based paging per-tenant
technical_notes: Index table schema: PK=(tenant_id, time_bucket, metric_route), clustering=(event_ts desc). Store event pointer (segment_id:int, offset:int) and summary fields used for aggregates to support partial aggregations without reading full events.
Time buckets: 0-7d -> 1h buckets; 8-30d -> 6h buckets; 31-90d -> 24h buckets. This reduces number of index entries for older ranges while preserving recent granularity.
Cursor token structure: base64(version|tenant_hash|segment_id|segment_offset|expiry_unix|signature). Signature uses service key to prevent tampering.
Prefetch knobs: initial N=2 blocks, backoff multiplier based on observed miss rate. Expose metrics for prefetch hit/miss and average prefetch latency.
Planner heuristics: estimated_events = tenant_cardinality_estimate * time_range_weight. If estimated_events > threshold -> use indexed-segment scan. Threshold tunable via runtime config.
Index TTL/compaction: per-time-bucket TTL configured per tenant class (free/paid/enterprise). Compact small lists into bloom filters to quickly answer existence queries for low-cost routes.
Security: index entries may contain tenant_id and route; ensure KMS protection in Private deployments. Sensitive fields must be redacted before indexing if flagged (see privacy label).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge index schema + API changes behind feature flag. 2) Run indexer in staging to build indexes for 10 canary tenants. 3) Deploy query planner with canary flag enabled for canary tenants only. 4) Monitor latency/IO for 48h; iterate prefetch knobs. 5) Gradually increase canary cohort to 20%, 50%, then 100% for eligible tenants. 6) Enable UI toggle in Console for customers to opt into cursor paging; allow rollback to offset-based pagination via flag. 7) Run full backfill for remaining tenants during off-peak using rate-limited worker pool.
metrics_to_monitor: planner.fallback_rate (percent of queries using legacy offset)

comments: 2026-02-25 - Marcus Nguyen: Initial design write-up posted. Need feedback from storage infra on index storage cost and compaction strategy.
2026-02-27 - Lena Zhao: (storage infra) We estimate ~120GB additional index storage for 100 median tenants with current bucket scheme; recommend adding bloom filter option for low-cardinality routes.
2026-03-02 - Sofia Martinez: Implementing cursor serializer and prefetch worker prototype. Running local benchmarks showing p95 improvement ~45% for synthetic heavy-tenant tests.
2026-03-05 - Priya Rao (SRE): Add health checks for prefetch worker; need circuit breaker to avoid cascading overload when index table has transient unavailability.

2026-03-09 - Sofia Martinez: Canary deploy started for 6 tenants. Observed planner fallback_rate ~12% for tenants with incomplete index coverage. Backfill job needs to prioritize active tenants first.
2026-03-11 - Marcus Nguyen: Decided to increase cursor expiry to 24h for enterprise tenants and 6h for free tier to reduce stale resource usage. Added runtime flag to override.
2026-03-12 - Sofia Martinez: Opened github draft PR for index migrations and basic planner; marking In Progress and starting QA test cases for cursor expiry and tamper protection.
